original_question: Let 1 < p < ∞ with p ≠ 2, and let μ be a finite measure such that the Banach space L^p(μ) is non-separable. Can L^p(μ) occur as a subspace of some Banach space that has an unconditional basis?
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact mathematical target of the paper almost verbatim: the parameter range 1 < p < ∞ with p ≠ 2, the assumption that μ is a finite measure, the non-separability of L^p(μ), and the embedding question into a Banach space with an unconditional basis. This is precisely the content of Problem 1.1.
missing_details: The paper works throughout over real Banach spaces.
In the paper, “subspace” means a closed linear subspace.
Because the ambient Banach space may be non-separable, “unconditional basis” is meant in the natural generalized sense for possibly non-separable Banach spaces.
To remove ambiguity, the question is best phrased as asking whether some Banach space with unconditional basis contains a copy of L^p(μ), i.e. a closed subspace isomorphic to L^p(μ).
No additional structure on the underlying measure space is assumed beyond μ being finite.
refined_question: Let 1 < p < ∞ with p ≠ 2, and let μ be a finite measure on an arbitrary measurable space such that L^p(μ) is non-separable. Does there exist a real Banach space having an unconditional basis (in the usual generalized sense for possibly non-separable spaces) that contains a closed linear subspace isomorphic to L^p(μ)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for such p and μ, can a Banach space with unconditional basis contain a copy of L^p(μ)?
justification: The draft matches the paper’s official formulation almost exactly: §1.1 states Problem 1.1 in essentially the same words. The nearby context explains that Enflo and Rosenthal proved the negative result under the stronger hypothesis dens(L^p(μ)) ≥ ℵ_ω and conjectured that the same conclusion should hold whenever L^p(μ) is merely non-separable, showing that this is the precise intended open problem rather than a broader neighboring one. The notation paragraph supplies the hidden conventions needed to make the question fully stand-alone: the paper considers real Banach spaces, and “subspace” means closed linear subspace; it also explicitly defines “contains a copy” as having an isomorphic subspace. The same §1.1 context notes that unconditional bases are being used in the natural non-separable extension.

citations.label: paper-wide conventions: real Banach spaces; subspace = closed linear subspace; “contains a copy” = has an isomorphic subspace
context preceding Problem 1.1: generalized unconditional bases for non-separable spaces; Enflo-Rosenthal theorem for dens(L^p(μ)) ≥ ℵ_ω; conjectured extension to all non-separable L^p(μ)
